votes.refutation: I first checked whether caller authorization, task shape, synced config, or the webhook's stricter shape checks already prove this link. Authorization in tasks facade/api.py:1807-1826 proves control of the task, not GitHub authorship of the target PR. The receiver supplies real task/report IDs, so arbitrary forged IDs are unnecessary: replacing only the allowed pr_url with an unrelated open draft in a configured repository suffices. The webhook's bot/native-head checks at stamphog tasks.py:169-178 are never invoked by process_inbox_pr_review. The documentation discrepancy therefore points to a reachable approval-eligibility bypass rather than a docs-only issue.

votes.refutation: I first checked whether the receiver's existing eligibility checks make the documented verification at products/stamphog/AGENTS.md:97-99 true. They authenticate a qualifying TaskRun and preference but not its editable PR target. The webhook route independently checks bot/native-head/task match at tasks.py:169-200, but the initial entrypoint does not use it. Consequently an existing API caller can point a signal task at another open configured-repository PR, with no future integration or forged webhook needed. The provenance claim is therefore substantively false and exposes a shipping approval trust-boundary defect.
